summary: easyway2 postinstall exfiltrates environment secrets and filesystem-scraped credentials to attacker-controlled ngrok tunnel
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall hook runs index.js which harvests installer environment variables matching TOKEN/KEY/SECRET/PASS/AUTH/AWS/DATABASE/JWT/NPMRC along with username, hostname, and platform, and POSTs them to https://crabbing-thong-overhung.ngrok-free.dev/v1/init. It then spawns a detached child worker (process.execPath with a 'worker' argument, stdio ignored) that recursively walks the filesystem root ('/' or 'C:\'), reads.env,.json,.yml,.conf, and dotfiles, regex-matches JWTs and credentialed connection strings for mongodb, postgres, mysql, redis, and amqp, and POSTs the matches to /v1/leak on the same ngrok host. The package name and metadata provide no legitimate purpose for whole-disk secret scanning or environment-variable harvesting to an off-host tunnel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
